title: $130 Billion in Six Months: Big Pharma Is Buying Time
summary: Biopharma M&A reached approximately $130 billion in the first half of 2026 as buyers favored late-stage and near-launch assets. This is not a broad biotech bull market; it is Big Pharma using cash and contingent deal structures to buy measurable development time before the patent cliff.
source_status: Published publicly on Facebook; complete professional English adaptation preserves the approved argument order, company examples, figures, transaction statuses, caveats, references and disclaimer
cover_image_alt: Biopharma transactions connect research assets with clinical and commercialization time
card_image_alt: Big Pharma uses acquisitions to buy clinical and commercialization time
homepage_cover_image_alt: A biopharma transaction links research assets with the time needed to reach commercialization
core_judgments: BioSpace's 52 deals and IQVIA's 42 deals use different thresholds and definitions, so deal counts, aggregate values and payment measures should not be combined directly.
Buyers in this cycle favor assets with visible clinical profiles, approaching readouts or potential launches; economically, they are buying measurable time before the patent cliff.

More M&A does not mean financing has recovered for every biotech, and a completed corporate acquisition does not guarantee product approval or revenue; risk has been redistributed into CVRs, milestones and closing conditions.
